stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs End Nine-Day Inflow Streak as Ether ETFs Keep Gaining
stories.summary: Decrypt reported that US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted net outflows after nine straight days of inflows. Ethereum ETFs extended their own inflow streak over the same period. The report did not give exact flow numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows show institutional demand for Bitcoin and Ether. A shift from Bitcoin to Ether funds can signal a change in investor sentiment.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin ETF outflows continue or reverse
Whether Ethereum ETF inflows keep pace
questions: What caused the Bitcoin outflow day?
How large were the flows in dollar terms?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs Snap Nine-Day Inflow Streak as Ethereum Funds Extend Their Run

stories.title: Hodler's Digest: Bitcoin's New Quantum Defenses and an 18.9M SOL Cancellation
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's Hodler's Digest covers two items this week: new quantum-resistance defenses for Bitcoin, and a cancelled allocation of 18.9 million SOL tokens. The digest bundles several smaller crypto news items into one weekly roundup. The report gives limited detail beyond these headlines.
stories.whyItMatters: Quantum-resistance work affects Bitcoin's long-term security. A large token cancellation affects Solana's supply.
whatToWatch: Further detail on the Bitcoin quantum-defense changes
Confirmation of the SOL cancellation and its effect on supply
questions: What specific quantum defenses were added to Bitcoin?
Why was the 18.9M SOL allocation cancelled?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s new quantum defenses, 18.9M SOL cancelled: Hodler’s Digest

stories.title: Mid-Tier Bitcoin Treasury Firm Bets Entire BTC Reserve on One 30-Day Reset Price
stories.summary: A mid-tier corporate Bitcoin treasury firm tied its entire BTC reserve to one price, set on a 30-day reset. CryptoSlate reported this and called it a concentrated bet rather than a hedge. The report did not name the company.
stories.whyItMatters: Corporate treasuries that hold large Bitcoin positions can worsen market swings. A forced sale at a set price can spread through the market.
whatToWatch: What happens when the 30-day reset date arrives
Whether other treasury firms adopt or avoid similar structures
questions: Which company made this bet?
What triggers a forced sale if the reset price is missed?

sources.title: One mid-tier Bitcoin treasury just gambled its entire BTC reserve on a single 30-day reset price

stories.title: Circle's Allaire Touts 'Internet Financial System' Platform as cirBTC Holds Just 40 BTC
stories.summary: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Circle built "the platform for the internet financial system." CryptoSlate reported this alongside a separate fact: Circle's cirBTC product holds only 40 BTC. The report highlights the gap between Allaire's stated ambition and the product's small size.
stories.whyItMatters: Circle is a major stablecoin issuer. Its move into Bitcoin-linked products shows how far it wants to expand beyond USDC.
whatToWatch: Whether cirBTC's BTC holdings grow
Any further comments from Allaire on Circle's Bitcoin strategy
questions: Why does cirBTC hold so little BTC relative to Circle's ambitions?
What is cirBTC's intended use case?

sources.title: CEO Jeremy Allaire says Circle built “the platform for the internet financial system”, but cirBTC has only 40 BTC

stories.title: Strategy's Bitcoin Holdings Show $2.8 Billion Profit — Is Saylor Planning Another Buy?
stories.summary: Strategy's Bitcoin holdings show $2.8 billion in unrealized profit, Decrypt reported. The report asks whether Michael Saylor plans another purchase. No new buy has been confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: Strategy holds one of the largest corporate Bitcoin positions. Its buying pattern can shift market sentiment and sometimes price.
whatToWatch: Any new Strategy purchase announcement
Saylor's public statements on further buys
questions: Will Strategy sell any of the profit or hold?
What would trigger a new purchase?

sources.title: Strategy’s Bitcoin Is $2.8 Billion in Profit—Is Saylor Teeing Up a Buy?

stories.title: Polygon Quietly Patched Security Flaws in Two Hard Forks Before Disclosure
stories.summary: Polygon fixed security flaws through two hard forks before it disclosed them publicly, Decrypt reported. This is a patch-first, disclose-later approach. The report did not give detail on the specific flaws.
stories.whyItMatters: Undisclosed flaws in a major network raise questions about transparency. Users faced unknown risk before the fix.
whatToWatch: Full technical disclosure of the patched flaws
Community reaction to the delayed disclosure
questions: What were the specific vulnerabilities?
Was any user fund or data at risk before the patch?

sources.title: Polygon Quietly Patched Security Flaws in Two Hard Forks Before Disclosing Them

stories.title: Saylor Signals Strategy Is 'Back' to Buying Bitcoin
stories.summary: Michael Saylor signaled that Strategy will resume buying Bitcoin, Cointelegraph reported. This follows a pause in new purchases. The report gave no purchase amount or date.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors watch Strategy's buying closely. It signals corporate demand for Bitcoin.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of a new Strategy Bitcoin purchase
Size and timing of any announced buy
questions: How large will the next purchase be?
What prompted the pause before this signal?

sources.title: Saylor signals Strategy is ‘Back’ to Bitcoin buying

stories.title: Russia's Sber Eyes USDT Loans, Questions Demand for the Digital Ruble
stories.summary: Russian bank Sber is looking at loans denominated in USDT, Cointelegraph reported. The bank also questioned demand for the digital ruble, Russia's central bank digital currency. The report gave no timeline for a USDT loan product.
stories.whyItMatters: A major Russian bank is looking at a dollar-pegged stablecoin. At the same time, it doubts its own government's digital currency. This shows tension between state CBDC plans and stablecoin demand.
whatToWatch: Any formal Sber USDT loan product launch
Russian regulatory response to bank use of USDT
Digital ruble adoption data
questions: How would Sber offer USDT loans under Russian law?
Why is digital ruble demand weak?

sources.title: Russia’s Sber eyes USDT loans, questions digital ruble demand

stories.title: Proposed Treasury Rule Under GENIUS Act Would Force US Exchanges to Audit Foreign Stablecoins or Delist Them
stories.summary: The US Treasury proposed a change to GENIUS Act rules. Under the change, US exchanges must audit foreign stablecoins or remove them from listings, CryptoSlate reported. The report did not give the audit standard or a timeline.
stories.whyItMatters: This proposal could change which stablecoins US exchanges list. It may favor US-regulated issuers over foreign ones.
whatToWatch: Formal rule text and comment period
Which foreign stablecoins are affected
Exchange responses and compliance timelines
questions: What audit standard would exchanges need to meet?
Which stablecoins count as 'foreign' under the proposal?

sources.title: Treasury proposed GENIUS change forces US exchanges to audit foreign stablecoin or face delisting

stories.title: Former White House Teleprompter Operator Fined for Prediction Market Insider Trading
stories.summary: A former White House teleprompter operator was fined for insider trading on a prediction market, Decrypt reported. The case involves trades based on non-public information tied to the operator's role. The report did not give the fine amount or the platform name.
stories.whyItMatters: This case shows regulators now enforce insider-trading rules on prediction markets. Prediction markets are a growing part of the crypto-adjacent industry.
whatToWatch: Full details of the enforcement action
Whether other prediction market insider cases follow
questions: How much was the fine?
Which prediction market platform was involved?

sources.title: Ex-White House Teleprompter Operator Fined for Prediction Market Insider Trading

stories.title: US Treasury Leans on Stablecoins for Short-Term Debt, But They Can't Fix a $28B Long-Bond Problem
stories.summary: The US Treasury relies more on stablecoin issuers to fund short-term debt, CryptoSlate reported. This demand does not fix a separate $28 billion long-bond funding problem, per the report. The report gave no further detail on the long-bond issue beyond this figure.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoin issuers such as Circle and Tether now buy meaningful amounts of US short-term debt. This ties crypto market health more closely to US Treasury funding.
whatToWatch: Treasury's approach to the long-bond funding gap
Stablecoin issuers' Treasury holdings data
questions: What exactly is the $28 billion long-bond problem?
Could stablecoin demand extend to longer-dated debt?

sources.title: US treasury relies on stablecoins to fund short-term debt, but they can’t fix its $28B long-bond problem

stories.title: A Leading Bitcoin Broker Exits Institutional Trading to Chase Power-Hungry Compute Deals
stories.summary: A leading Bitcoin brokerage stepped back from institutional trading, CryptoSlate reported. It now pursues deals tied to large-scale power capacity. The report frames this as a pivot toward gigawatt-scale power needs. The report did not name the firm.
stories.whyItMatters: This shift shows how power and compute demand now shape crypto business models. Trading volume is no longer the only driver.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of which firm made this move and its new focus
New power-related deals or partnerships announced
questions: Which broker is this?
What kind of power deals are being pursued — mining, AI data centers, or both?

sources.title: Wall Street’s favorite Bitcoin broker just walked away from institutional trading to chase gigawatts of power
